chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Ella Fitzgerald album with Benny Carter and Georgie Auld
summary: He recounts a recent Capitol album with Ella and Carter's all-star group, thirty tunes segued without a break, including a Hawaiian War Chant single.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You were saying earlier that someone who you recorded with wasn't stimulating musically. Who were some that you recorded with of the most stimulating people, musically, (inaudible).

Well, I was telling you about one recording I did with Ella Fitzgerald about -- I guess about two years ago. This was a unique, unusual record in that we did 30 tunes on one side, and we segued from one tune to another, never a break, just a direct segue. And it was a beautiful album. Benny Carter was the leader, and it was Georgie Auld, Edison Georgia All, Harry Sweets Addison, and Louie Bellson. We had a bass player, Bob West. Did I say Jimmie Jones was playing piano? Yeah, Jimmie Jones was playing piano. And I think Panama was on this -- Panama Francis, yeah. That's right, re-
mind me about the last names because I --
Most of the Times us (inaudible) we've used first names that are so well known --

Yes, so you know, I forget. But any way this was an unusual recording, and for me it was like Georgie Auld homecoming because I hadn't seen Georgie Auld, and -- nor worked with him in so long, since -- actually I hadn't worked with him since the Street. Now, you know what the street is, 52nd Street. Okay, now -- and Georgie -- he's a giant. You know, the warmth there, it was just-- I mean, musically the warmth of there was just permeating the whole studio. So it was kind of a nice thing. And they took a lot of these tunes out and made singles, and we did a Hawaiian War Chant, and this was electric.
We got into a thing -- they took this out of -- and put it out as a single. That was very -- I have quite a few solos on that.

No, no, this was for Bob Field, was that it. Yeah. We did it for Capitol. It was a kind of unique idea, you know. But I had quite a few solos on that that I liked, but Pat, I am going to do some recording very soon and I'm going to do quite a few things that I like, you know.
